heads._what: How each MACULA phrase rule is read by the clean builder (stage S1). Data, not code (docs/BUILDER-DESIGN.md). Each rule is one KIND: coord (every conjunct is a member of a composite), head_first / head_last (the head, with the other children as its dependents under the named relation), prep (a preposition and its object: the object is the filler, the preposition goes on the edge), wrap (one child, transparent). A rule not listed: MACULA's explicit head mark if it has one, else the first child. Surveyed 2026-09-27: 210 phrase rules; the ones below cover the great majority of groups.
heads._null: A null relation (the article, the object marker) makes no edge: the word is structural, and its morpheme is claimed by the head it marks.

lexicon._what: Function words for the clean builder (stages S2 and S3). Data, not code. Keys are consonants only (points and accents removed).
lexicon._phrases: Keys with spaces are MACULA's connective phrases (class cjp), keyed by every word including a preposition, so עַל־כֵּן 'therefore' is not read as a lone כֵּן 'so'. A phrase with no key of its own falls back to its last word that has one (וְגַם, וְעַתָּה -> the waw's 'and'). וְעַתָּה is left 'and': MACULA glosses it 'therefore' 144 times and 'now' 125, and the form does not decide which.
lexicon._speech: speech_verbs frame a speech turn (S4); after perceive_verbs a כִּי is 'that' (content), not 'because' (S3). Lists from the old builder, where each was checked against the corpus's own lemma spellings.
lexicon._notes: fused: a waw on a wayyiqtol or weqatal is inside the verb ('and then'). verse_initial: a כִּי that opens a verse is 'for' OR 'when' by form, so the link is written as undecided with both candidates (2026-09-27: marked undecided). within_by_prep: a clause nested under a preposition takes the relation the preposition carries; the rest stay 'within'.
lexicon._aramaic: The Aramaic of Daniel, Ezra and Jer 10:11 is in MACULA's Hebrew files and read with this table (2026-09-27). Its verb forms share the Hebrew names (qatal, yiqtol, participle), its negatives and questions the same marks. Its own words land on the shared kinds: הֵן 'if', לָהֵן and בְּרַם 'but', כְּדִי 'when', כָּל־קֳבֵל דִּי 'because', דִּי 'that' after a verb of perceiving, and the narrative's אֱדַיִן / בֵּאדַיִן 'then' as the same `then` the Hebrew wayyiqtol carries.

heads._what: How each MACULA GREEK phrase rule is read by the clean builder (stage S1): the same kinds as tables/hebrew/heads.json, so the two languages build the same structure. MACULA marks NO heads in the Greek (surveyed 2026-09-27: 168 rules, 0 head marks), so every convention is here. Clause COMPLEXES (Conj-CL, sub-CL, that-VP, CLaCL, ClCl, aCLaCL, notCLbutCL2CL ...) need no entry: a group holding only connectives and clauses is read as a complex whatever its rule. `2Advp_h1` / `2Advp_h2` name their own head.
heads._greek_only: Kept, not dropped: `periphrastic` (a form of εἰμί with a participle, BeVerb / VerbBe) and `demonstrative`; the article (DetNP) is structural like the Hebrew article.

lexicon._what: Greek function words for the clean builder (stages S2-S4): the SAME kinds as tables/hebrew/lexicon.json, so a Greek purpose link is the same `purpose` as a Hebrew one. Keys are accent-free lower case. What Greek marks that Hebrew does not is kept as an attribute on the shared kind (2026-09-27: where Greek does things that Hebrew cannot, it is good to show it, but in a way that the core structures align).
lexicon._subjunctive: A subjunctive in a main clause, with no subordinating connective, is hortatory or prohibitive ('let us go', 'do not ...'): directive, like the Hebrew cohortative and jussive. Under ἵνα, ἐάν, ὅταν and the like it is dependent, and the clause's force is set by its host.
lexicon._question: Nestle 1904 prints the Greek question mark (;). Like the BSB's quotation marks it is an editor's structure, not the text's words (PRINCIPLES 44): used, and recorded as its source.
lexicon._within: A clause nested under a connective or a preposition takes the relation it carries; 'εἰς τό' + infinitive is purpose, 'διὰ τό' + infinitive reason, 'ἐν τῷ' + infinitive the time (the articular infinitive, which Hebrew has no form for, lands on the shared kinds). `if` is written condition -> consequence, as the Hebrew is. πρίν ('before') and μετὰ τό ('after') have no kind yet and stay `within`.
lexicon._letters: A letter is a Writing, as a psalm is: its opening names its writer in the nominative (Paul, James, Peter, Jude). The writer is the letter's voice, as the psalmist is the psalm's.
lexicon._narrative_then: Between two past-tense indicatives, καί and δέ carry the narrative's sequence: the same `then` the Hebrew wayyiqtol carries inside its verb (2026-09-28: 121 Greek `then` links against 20,177 Hebrew, so no sequence pattern could reach the New Testament).
lexicon._reflexive: Greek has reflexive pronouns of its own (ἑαυτοῦ, σεαυτοῦ, ἐμαυτοῦ), so a plain αὐτός in a clause is not that clause's subject (S5). Hebrew uses the plain pronoun reflexively and has no such entry.

hebrew._note: VerbX wraps a Hebrew verb stem and a trailing paragogic/cohortative suffix <w class='x'> (e.g. Gen 3:4 תְּמֻתֽוּן).
